# LE MÈTRE DES ARCHIVES
### *Or, The Decommissioning of the Neutral Axis*

#### *A Monograph, Dossier, and Confession by Dr. Alistair Finch-Vane*
*Second Conservator of Subterranean Standards, Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, Pavillon de Breteuil, Sèvres*
*Autumn, 1960*

---

```
BIPM / DOSSIER D’AMORTISSEMENT N° 60-XI-M
DESTINATAIRE: Comité International des Poids et Mesures (CIPM)
OBJET: Protocole de translation ontologique — Étalon Prototype International du Mètre (Alliage 1874: Pt-Ir 90/10) vers la radiation orangée de l’atome de Krypton-86 (λ = 6057,80211 Å).
LOCALISATION: Crypte du Pavillon de Breteuil, Palier -3 (Chambre du Régulateur Isotherme).
AUTEUR: Dr. A. Finch-Vane, Conservateur Adjoint.
```

---

### MOVEMENT I: THE SUBTERRANEAN FOUNDRY

```
[FIGURE 1.1: ARCHIVAL SCHEMATIC — BARS IN TRANSIT]
Plan of Vault Level -3 beneath the Saint-Cloud escarpment.
Cross-section through Lutetian limestone bedrock (Calcaire grossier).
Airy-point supports (a = L / √3 ≈ 0.5773 L) indicated along the neutral horizontal rib of the Tresca section.
Thermal insulation: Triple-walled zinc coffer, paraffin bath, dry nitrogen cushion.
```

The foundations of the Pavillon de Breteuil do not rest upon the earth as buildings commonly do, but are sunk into the damp, calcified marrow of the Saint-Cloud escarpment like the teeth of an archaic anchor that has caught, once and for all, in the limestone detritus of an exhausted sea. 

When I descended this morning at five o’clock—carrying the three keys whose bitted iron profiles have, since the presidency of Patrice de MacMahon, maintained the sovereign fiction of an immovable world—the air within the shaft had already assumed that specific, leaden equilibrium that belongs only to spaces excavated forty meters beneath the reach of sunlight. It is an air devoid of weather; an atmosphere without seasons, without barometric respiration, preserved at an artificial, unvarying temperature of zero degrees Celsius by the continuous circulation of brine through jacketed lead conduits. In this vault, the passage of decades is registered not by the accumulation of dust or the yellowing of parchment, but by the infinitesimal, almost imperceptible creeping of metal: the slow, molecular settling of platinum atoms as they accommodate themselves to the geometry of Henri Tresca’s cross-section.

For thirty-two years, Arthur, I have descended these thirty-six steps of damp Meudon stone with the lantern suspended from my left hand, holding its wick low so that the combustion of the kerosene might not introduce a thermal plume of even one-thousandth of a degree into the micro-climate of the chamber. You will recall—if the dead retain any recollection of the physical agonies of calibration—how we used to speak of these subterranean vaults during our long seasons in the Syrian desert, when the British Imperial Mandate’s cadastral survey required us to stretch our hundred-meter invar bands across the cracked mudflats of the Hauran. You said then, wiping the alkaline dust from the vernier scale of your Troughton & Simms theodolite, that every boundary line we drew between the administrative sand and the olive groves of the fellahin was an act of violence against the continuity of the earth; and that the only innocent surveyor was the one who worked in the dark, measuring nothing but the distance between a diamond scratch and a human eye.

```
EXTRACT: JOURNAL DE CONSERVATION (FINCH-VANE), 14 SEPTEMBRE 1960.
Material verification of Prototype No. 6.
Alloy composition: 89.98% Platinum, 10.02% Iridium.
Density at 0°C: 21.546 g/cm³.
Cross-section: Modified X-form (Tresca design), height 20 mm, width 20 mm.
Condition of specular facets: No oxidation; microscopic striations visible on the polished neutral plane.
Diamond fiducial engravings (a, b, c): Sharpness intact; lateral drift undetectable within the mechanical tolerance of the comparator (± 0.02 µm).
Observations: Ambient mechanical noise increased due to preparatory excavations for the cryogenic interferometer installation in Vault -2.
```

To preserve the prototype, one must first master the art of non-existence. One does not enter the presence of the bar as a man enters a room; one enters as a potential source of parasitic heat, an engine of thermodynamic disturbance that must be muffled, deflected, and neutralized. 

Before I am permitted to unseal the outer safe—the iron doors of which were cast by the foundry of Schneider-Creusot in the winter of 1888, with double-tongued mortise locks that engage into the rock with the dull, oil-soaked thud of a guillotine carriage—I must spend twenty minutes in the intermediate antechamber. There, I strip myself of my woolens, my leather boots, my horn-rimmed spectacles, and my watch. The watch is an iron-cased pocket chronometer by Dent of London; its balance spring, though compensated for temperature, contains within its hair-thin spiral of tempered steel a tiny, erratic pulse of magnetism that the comparator’s iron frame might feel as an alien force. I put on the linen smock, boiled until its fibers are limp and free of sizing; the felt slippers with soles of unvulcanized rubber; and the long mica shield that straps across the lower half of the face to direct the moist, thirty-seven-degree exhaust of human respiration upward and backward, away from the optical axis of the microscopes.

It was Henri Tresca who understood that if a bar of metal is supported along its entire length by a flat bed, the friction between its lower face and the support will prevent it from contracting and expanding freely with the rise and fall of the seasons, storing within its crystalline matrix a reserve of elastic tension that will, over years, warp the line of its truth. And if it is supported only at its extreme ends, its own dead weight—the sheer, downward pull of its twenty-one grams per cubic centimeter—will cause its middle to sag, stretching the upper surface and compressing the lower. 

His solution was a masterwork of nineteenth-century metallurgical mechanics, an X-shaped profile whose symmetry is not merely aesthetic, but functional: an architecture of resistance designed so that the neutral fiber—the theoretical plane within the metal that undergoes neither elongation nor compression when the bar flexes—is brought to the surface, exposed to the light, polished like a dark mirror, and inscribed with three parallel lines whose width does not exceed five microns.

Those lines, Arthur. You remember them. When you held the diamond scriber in the workshop behind the Damascus Gate in 1937, attempting to recalibrate the steel chains we had dragged through the salt marshes of the Dead Sea, you told me that a line drawn by a diamond in an alloy of platinum is the closest humanity has ever come to an absolute pact with the ground. The diamond does not remove metal; it plows it. It pushes the platinum aside into two microscopic, lateral ridges—two tiny banks of dark earth thrown up along the margin of a furrow. And between those two banks lies the ditch: the absence where the light does not reflect, the narrow, bottomless black groove that separates *here* from *there*, the sovereign territory of the meter from the wild, unmeasured chaos of the universe.

Now, they tell me, the furrow is an embarrassment. 

In the upper rooms of the Pavillon, where the young men from the *Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt* and the National Physical Laboratory walk about in their white nylon coats, drinking instant coffee and whistling through their teeth, they speak of the Tresca bar as though it were a stone idol dragged from an Assyrian tumulus—a clumsy, lumpy, oxidized stick of grease and metal whose length depends upon the whim of the Paris weather, the level of the water table beneath the Seine, and the thickness of the oil on the screws of the comparator.

"The bar," Dr. Ernst Meyer told me yesterday, tapping his plastic fountain pen against the glass of the barometer in the library, "is an anachronism of the artisanal age, Finch-Vane. It is an individual. It has an autobiography. It suffers from fatigue; it remembers the hammer blows of 1874; it expands when an omnibus rumbles over the bridge at Sèvres; it contracts when the ice in the cellars begins to melt. How can you base an international system of units upon an object that possesses a memory? Science requires an étalon that has no history, no mass, no skin, and no grave."

He did not look at me when he said this. He was looking through the tall French windows at the park of Saint-Cloud, where the chestnuts were dropping their leaves into the yellow mud of the avenues. He was looking at the future: a glass tube filled with a rare, inert gas, excited by a radio-frequency discharge until it glows with the pale, sickly orange light of a dying coal; a beam of light split in two by a half-silvered mirror, traveling through an absolute vacuum, reflecting against quartz plates, and recombining to form an immaterial staircase of interference fringes that can be counted by an electronic eye without a single human finger ever having to touch a vernier or peer through a filar micrometer.

"Sixteen hundred and fifty thousand, seven hundred and sixty-three point seven three wavelengths," he murmured, his fingers twitching in his pockets like a gambler calculating the odds on a turn of the card. "In vacuo. The $2p_{10} - 5d_5$ transition of Krypton-86. It is identical in Sèvres, in Teddington, in Leningrad, and on the surface of the moon. It does not wear out. It cannot be dropped. It cannot be stolen by the Communards or buried in a zinc tube beneath the cellar floor during a Prussian bombardment."

I did not answer him. I took up my ledger—the calfskin-bound folio whose pages have grown soft and gray at the edges like the ears of an old dog—and turned back toward the stairs. But as I closed the heavy baize door behind me, I thought of our survey at Safad in the spring of forty-eight. 

We had used an old steel tape that had been calibrated in Cairo before the first war; its coefficient of expansion was unknown, its surface was pitted with rust from the damp nights in the olive groves, and its zero-mark had been repaired with a brass rivet by a blacksmith in Acre. Because of that rivet, Arthur—because that brass joint was three-tenths of a millimeter thicker than the steel ribbon it joined—the line we traced between the mandate boundary and the village cemetery fell four yards to the west of the dry-stone wall that the Mukhtar had shown us on his grandfather’s map. 

Four yards. A distance you could cross in three strides. But when the guns began to fire from the ridge two weeks later, those three strides were the difference between the cellar of the schoolhouse and the open field where the armored cars were turning in the dust. The men who died there did not die of politics; they died of the thermal expansion of an uncompensated ribbon of Sheffield steel under a Syrian sun.

And now Meyer wants to tell me that measurement is an angel without weight.

---

The light from the Krypton tube does not illuminate the room; it drains it of blood.

It has been installed in the lower laboratory, in Vault -2, which was once the storage room for the standard hydrometers and the balance of Rueprecht. The heavy mahogany cases, with their counterpoises of gilded brass and their agate knife-edges bedded in rock crystal, have all been pushed against the wall and covered with gray rubberized sheets, like the furniture in a manor house whose owners have died without heirs. 

In their place, mounted upon a slab of black Swedish granite that rests upon four pneumatic cylinders, stands the interferometer.

It is an apparatus without joints, without gears, without screws that can be turned by a hand wearing a glove. It is a cluster of brass barrels, copper cooling coils, and glass tubes through which liquid nitrogen boils with a faint, dry hiss like the breathing of an adder in a stone wall. When Meyer turns the rheostat, the gas inside the capillary tube ignites.

It is not the yellow, smoky light of the paraffin lamps with which we worked in our youth, nor the white, hard, diamond brilliance of the arc lamps that the French engineers used when they surveyed the tunnels for the underground railway beneath Montmartre. It is an unnatural, cold, monochromatic orange—a color that does not exist anywhere in the mineral world, a wavelength ripped from the electron shells of an odorless gas that has been squeezed until it can do nothing but scream at a frequency of five hundred million megacycles per second.

Under this light, the skin of my hands does not look like flesh; it looks like slate. The mahogany tables lose their warmth and become blocks of charred timber; the brass screws of the comparators turn the color of dried liver; and the ink on the ruled pages of my logbook turns from blue to a greasy, impenetrable violet.

```
EXTRACT: JOURNAL DE CONSERVATION (FINCH-VANE), 28 SEPTEMBRE 1960.
The transition work advances. Today, the optical team under Dr. Meyer completed the comparison of the primary quartz etalon (200 mm) against the wavelength of the orange line of Krypton-86.
Refractive index correction applied for residual nitrogen in the optical chamber:
    n(air) - 1 = [6432.8 + 2949810 / (146 - σ²) + 25540 / (41 - σ²)] × 10⁻⁸
Barometric compensation: Manual reading from the Tonnelot mercury column abandoned in favor of the differential capacitance transducer.
The observer’s eye is no longer placed at the ocular of the filar microscope. The fringes are counted by a photomultiplier tube (RCA-1P21) coupled to a decade scaler.
Note on personal health: A peculiar fatigue of the eyes. An inability to fix the names of the small instruments upon the lower bench. The brass tool used for the lateral alignment of the rollers—the one with the knurled head and the left-handed thread—I could not name it this morning when speaking to the apprentice. I called it "the cylindrical mass with the radial ridges." He looked at me with an expression of insolence.
```

Arthur, the nouns are beginning to peel away from the world down here.

It began three weeks ago, on the day they disconnected the refrigeration pipes from the long trough of Prototype No. 6. I went to the tool board—the oak board that Henri Tresca himself seasoned in linseed oil and mounted on the northern pillar in 1882—to reach for the long, flat steel instrument with the boxwood handle that we have always used to scrape the frost from the observation windows of the comparator. You know the one: its blade is ground with a forty-five-degree bevel on the forward edge, and the wood of the grip has been darkened by the sweat of five generations of conservators until it looks like bog oak.

I looked at it. I reached out my hand. But the word for it—the simple, monosyllabic name that every boy who has ever worked in a joiner’s shop knows before he is seven years old—had vanished from my mind like a drop of ether spilled on a hot plate. 

I saw its length: two hundred and forty millimeters. I saw its cross-section: five millimeters of tempered carbon steel, hardened at the tip to approximately 60 Rockwell C. I saw its refractive properties under the orange discharge of the Krypton lamp, noting that its specular reflection coefficient was roughly 0.42. I felt the dry, fibrous texture of the wood against the pad of my thumb, and I calculated that the moisture content of the handle must have fallen below eight percent owing to the continuous dehumidification of the vault. 

But its *name*—that heavy, blunt, peasant name that anchors the blade to the floor of human speech—was gone. 

In its place, my mind offered only a series of spatial coordinates and differential equations: an account of the volume of air it displaced within the chamber ($V \approx 48.6 \text{ cm}^3$), the thermal hysteresis of its blade when carried from the antechamber to the comparator bed ($\Delta L = L_0 \cdot \alpha \cdot \Delta T$), and the optical absence it created against the whitewashed limestone of the wall.

I stood there for five minutes, my arm extended, my fingers hovering over the hooks, until Meyer came up behind me.

"Are you looking for the scraper, Finch-Vane?" he asked, and took it down with a single, careless jerk of his wrist.

*The scraper.* The word sounded monstrous to me: an ugly, guttural, Germanic agglomeration of consonants that had no relation whatever to the cold, flat blade of steel that hung between his thumb and forefinger. It was too small for it; it was too coarse. It was like trying to measure the diameter of a planetary orbit with a shoemaker’s rule.

"Yes," I said, through the mica mask. "The implement for the mechanical removal of the crystalline phase of water."

He laughed, thinking I was making a joke in the dry, pedantic manner of the English mandate officials with whom his father had served on the Boundary Commissions of the League of Nations. But I was not joking. I was terrified.

Since that morning, the disease has spread from the tool board to the rest of the laboratory. It is as if the installation of the optical standard has initiated an epistemological evaporation—a slow, silent process of sub-atomic sublimation that is dissolving the material names of things, leaving behind only their geometric envelopes, their optical signatures, and their thermodynamic capacities.

The heavy table of Ardesian slate upon which the balance stands is no longer a *table*; it is an *inertial mass of high damping capacity, presenting an upper horizontal plane at an elevation of 820 millimeters above the datum of the floor*. The bronze carriage that carries the microscope along the rail is no longer a *carriage*; it is a *mechanical translation stage with two degrees of freedom, subject to a parasitic pitch error of three arcseconds per decimeter of travel*. 

And the bar itself...

Yesterday, when I entered the inner crypt to prepare Prototype No. 6 for its final comparison against the working standard of the Conservatoire, I looked into the zinc coffer where it has rested upon its two Bénoît rollers since the year of my birth. 

I looked down at the specular facets. I looked at the three diamond scratches at the right-hand end—the scratches that define the limit of human terrestrial movement, the boundary of the field, the length of the road from Jerusalem to Jericho, the height of the walls of Acre, the span of the bridges over the Rhine.

I could no longer see the platinum.

I did not see a bar of metal forged by Johnson, Matthey & Co. in the Hatton Garden foundry, hammered on an anvil of cast iron, drawn through a die of hardened steel, and polished with the dust of rottenstone and olive oil. I saw only a linear vacancy in the limestone: a corridor of zero-displacement forty millimeters square and one thousand and twenty millimeters long, along whose axis the speed of light in a vacuum would experience a delay of exactly $3.33564 \times 10^{-9}$ seconds.

The metal had become a ghost before they had even unscrewed it from its mount.

---

```
[MINUTES OF THE SUB-COMMITTEE ON THE REDEFINITION OF THE METRE]

"The General Conference...
Considering that the international Prototype does not provide a standard of the metre capable of a precision adequate for the present needs of metrology,
Decides:
1. The metre is the length equal to 1,650,763.73 wavelengths in vacuum of the radiation corresponding to the transition between the levels 2p₁₀ and 5d₅ of the atom of krypton-86..."
```

### MOVEMENT III: THE EPISTEMOLOGICAL VOID

```
BIPM / DOSSIER D’AMORTISSEMENT N° 60-XI-M (SUITE)
SECTION FINALE: DEPOSITAIRE DES ARCHIVES
CHAMBRE SOUTERRAINE DU PAVILLON DE BRETEUIL (PALIER -3)
12 OCTOBRE 1960, 23:40 HEURES.
```

The delegates have arrived in Paris.

From the window of the conservator's lodge at the gate of the park, I watched their black Citroëns climb the hill from the bridge of Sèvres this afternoon, their tires making a wet, tearing sound upon the fallen leaves of the plane trees. They come from everywhere: from the Bureau of Standards in Washington, from the Mendeleev Institute in Leningrad, from the National Research Council in Ottawa, from Tokyo, from Pretoria, from Teddington. They carry briefcases of pigskin and morocco leather, stuffed with the proofs of their interferometric tables, their fringe-counting circuits, their calculations of the Doppler broadening of the spectral lines of cadmium, mercury-198, and krypton-86.

They are all young, or they are men who have learned how to look young by casting off the weight of matter. They walk quickly. They do not look at the stone gateposts, where the Prussian shells left their pockmarks in the winter of 1870; they do not look at the moss that grows in the joints of the retaining wall, nor at the iron drainpipes that lead the water away from the foundations of the chateau. They are moving into an isotropic universe: an empty, transparent, frictionless space where distance is no longer something that must be walked over with heavy boots, but a numerical ratio between two energy states of an uncharged atom.

Tonight, the vaults are deserted. The optical team has gone to dinner at a brasserie in the Boulevard Saint-Germain to celebrate the printing of the draft resolution.

I am alone on Palier -3.

I have not lit the kerosene lantern. I do not need it. The orange discharge tube in the interferometer in Vault -2 has been left on to maintain thermal equilibrium before tomorrow’s demonstration, and its light leaks through the open bronze doorway like the glow from a furnace in which nothing is consumed.

I am sitting upon the... upon the *horizontal elevated plane of joinery supported by four vertical prismatics of ash*. (You see, Arthur? The word has gone entirely now. I can no longer find the four-letter monosyllable that denotes the thing upon which one writes. It has slipped off the edge of the world. If I try to reach for it, I find only the empty space between its legs and the acoustic resistance it offers to the echo of my breathing.)

In front of me, resting upon its two supports of polished steel—the *points of minimum flexure*, separated by precisely five hundred and seventy-one millimeters—lies the... the *linear metallurgical standard of modified X-form*.

It has no color under this orange sky. Its surface is neither silver nor gray; it is an absence of light that has taken the form of an X.

I lay my hand upon it.

I know that I am violating the protocol. I know that by touching the bar with the bare skin of my right index finger, I am introducing a thermal disturbance that will propagate through its crystalline lattice for forty-eight hours; that the heat of my blood ($T = 36.8^\circ\text{C}$) will cause the neutral fiber to expand by approximately zero point zero zero zero seven millimeters in the vicinity of the four-hundred-millimeter mark; that the diamond scratches at the ends will be thrown out of parallelism by a fraction of an arcsecond; and that tomorrow morning, when Meyer switches on his electronic counter, the instrument will detect an anomaly in the fringe field that he will attribute to an uncompensated pressure pulse from the Paris-Versailles railway line.

I do not care.

I press my finger down into the groove of the Tresca section. I want to feel the resistance of the metal. I want to feel the weight of the ninety percent platinum and the ten percent iridium: the heavy, cold, stubborn earth-stuff that was dug out of the gravels of the Ural mountains by men who worked with picks and shovels in the reign of Alexander the Second.

```

It does not feel cold. It feels like nothing at all.

The metal has attained such an exquisite thermal equilibrium with the subterranean rock that it has ceased to offer any sensation of temperature to the skin. It does not take heat from the finger, nor does it give it back. It is merely a boundary: an impenetrable geometric threshold beyond which the spatial coordinates cannot be extended.

And as I sit here, Arthur, in this vault where the walls have lost their stone and have become merely *the vertical limits of an excavation forty meters beneath the surface of the Lutetian plateau*, I realize that our entire lives were an error of the senses.

We believed that we were measuring the world. We believed that when we set up our three-legged brass supports in the wadi at sunset, when we leveled the spirit bubbles with the tips of our fingers, when we looked through the spider-silk reticules at the white-painted markers on the hills of Moab, we were participating in the great, patient ordering of a physical creation that God had left rough and unfinished so that draughtsmen might have a purpose in the world.

We thought the line was *there*—in the mud, in the chalk, in the iron, in the sweat that dried on the leather bands of our hats.

It was never there.

The line was only the gap between two wavelengths that had not yet been counted. It was an empty interval: a silence between two vibrations of an atom that does not know that France exists, that does not know that the Ottoman Empire fell, that does not know that the graves in the cemetery at Safad were dug four yards to the east of where they should have been.

Tomorrow, they will lift the bar from its rollers for the last time. They will place it in a coffer of plate glass—not to protect it from the air, but to protect the air from the bar. They will carry it up the thirty-six stone steps into the hall of honor, where the delegates will file past it on their way to the luncheon buffet, looking down at its Tresca cross-section with that peculiar, condescending pity that men who work with numbers reserve for things that can be broken by a hammer.

Meyer will deliver the report. He will show the slides: the black-and-white plates showing the interference patterns, the sharp, concentric rings of light and dark that look like the cross-section of an onion made of frost. He will speak of the error of the microscopic sighting—how the human eye can never decide, to within more than two-hundredths of a micron, where the center of a diamond furrow lies—and he will contrast this clumsy, human hesitation with the absolute, indifferent certainty of the decade scaler, which counts its one million, six hundred and fifty thousand, seven hundred and sixty-three fringes without ever having to decide anything at all.

And I?

I will sit at the back of the hall, near the radiator that rattles when the pressure drops in the boiler room. I will have my calfskin ledger open on my knees, but I will not write in it. 

I will have no words left to write.

I will look at the delegate from the United Kingdom—the young man with the mustache who has taken over our old office in the basement of the Ordnance Survey at Southampton—and if he asks me for the key to the iron safe in Vault -3, I will not be able to hand it to him.

I will be able only to open my hand and show him the *void of sixty-four cubic centimeters bounded by five articulating phalanges of ossified cartilage and epidermal tissue*.

I will show him the place where the key used to be, before it became a set of spatial intervals in an isotropic vacuum.

```
[CONCLUDING SCHEMATIC: BIPM DOSSIER 60-XI-M]
Final state of the Vault:
The Tresca standard No. 6 is removed from the comparator.
The optical axis is unobstructed.
The distance between the two reference mirrors (M₁, M₂) is measured exclusively in units of:
    L = N × (λ_Kr86 / 2)
Where N = 3,301,527.46
The error is zero.
The room is empty.
The temperature is zero.
The observer has been eliminated from the system.

The light in the discharge tube is flickering now.

The liquid nitrogen in the cooling reservoir must be running low; the vacuum pump in the corner is changing its pitch, its three-phase electric motor drawing an extra quarter of an ampere as the oil begins to cool in the sumps. The orange glow is retreating into the capillary, pulling its cold, unnatural radiation back from the walls, back from the slate table, back from the zinc coffer.

In a few moments, the gas will go out.

The vault will return to its proper state: not to darkness—for darkness is merely the absence of an optical frequency that can be detected by the rhodopsin in the rods of the retina—but to that pure, unmeasured, geometric silence that existed before Henri Tresca scratched his three lines in the platinum, and that will remain after the last bridge over the Seine has fallen into the mud of its own riverbed.

I am taking my finger off the bar now, Arthur.

The metal is expanding. The heat of my hand is traveling along the neutral axis toward the ends, pushing the two specular facets outward by fifty nanometers. 

Let it expand.

Let it stretch until it touches the limestone walls of the vault. Let it push through the foundations of the Pavillon de Breteuil, through the roots of the chestnut trees, through the clay of the park, through the houses of Sèvres, through the bridges, through the rivers, through the deserts where we left our chains to rust in the sand.

Let it become so long that no one will ever be able to count its wavelengths again.

### Problem: Non-Equilibrium Causal Identification and Dissipation Bounds in a Chiral Stochastic Biochemical Oscillator

Consider an open, non-equilibrium biochemical reaction network operating at steady state under constant temperature $T$ (with $\beta = (k_B T)^{-1}$). The system consists of three continuous mesoscopic chemical species with concentrations $\mathbf{X}(t) = (X_1(t), X_2(t), X_3(t))^\top \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^3$, governed by the coupled Langevin dynamics:

$$\frac{d X_i}{dt} = f_i(\mathbf{X}) + g_i(X_i) \xi_i(t), \quad i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$$

where $\xi_i(t)$ are mutually independent Gaussian white noise processes satisfying $\langle \xi_i(t) \xi_j(t') \rangle = 2 D_i \delta_{ij} \delta(t - t')$, and $g_i(X_i) = \sqrt{X_i}$.

The deterministic drift vector $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{X})$ is parameterized by reaction rate constants $\boldsymbol{\theta} = \{k_1, k_{-1}, k_2, k_{-2}, k_3, k_{-3}\}$ and an unobserved external chemical potential gradient $\Delta \mu_{U} \neq 0$ maintained by an unmeasured buffered substrate-product pool $U$:

$$\begin{aligned}
f_1(\mathbf{X}) &= k_1 X_3 e^{\alpha \Delta \mu_U} - k_{-1} X_1 X_2 \\
f_2(\mathbf{X}) &= k_2 X_1 - k_{-2} X_2 X_3 \\
f_3(\mathbf{X}) &= k_3 X_2 - k_{-3} X_3 e^{-(1-\alpha)\Delta \mu_U}
\end{aligned}$$

where $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ denotes the kinetic transition-state symmetry factor. 

In addition to the mesoscopic Langevin coordinates, an experimentalist possesses:
1. Passive observational time-series data $\mathcal{D}_{\text{obs}} = \{ \mathbf{X}(t) \}_{t \in [0, \mathcal{T}]}$ in the non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) with stationary probability density $P_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})$.
2. A single soft local clamping intervention $\text{do}(X_2 = c)$, where $X_2$ is rigidly pinned to a constant value $c > 0$ via a feedback-controlled microfluidic trap, while the unobserved reservoir $U$ continues to drive the cycle asynchronously.

---

#### Part 1: Structural Causal Identification under Hidden Non-Equilibrium Driving

Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the directed acyclic graph (DAG) obtained by time-unrolling the infinitesimal generator over time slices $t \to t + dt$.

1. Using Pearl's do-calculus and the Framework of Stochastic Differential Equations with latent Markovian states, prove whether the interventional probability density $P(\mathbf{X}_{\setminus \{2\}}(t + \tau) \mid \text{do}(X_2(t) = c))$ is non-parametrically identifiable from the observational distribution $P_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})$ and the known graph topology without measuring $\Delta \mu_U$. 
2. Explicitly derive the expression for the average causal effect $\frac{\partial}{\partial c} \mathbb{E}[X_1 \mid \text{do}(X_2 = c)]_{\text{NESS}}$ in terms of the stationary probability current density $\mathbf{J}_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})$ and the conditional score function $\nabla_{\mathbf{X}} \ln P_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})$.

---

#### Part 2: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations (TUR) under Causal Interventions

Define the stationary entropy production rate (EPR) of the unperturbed system as:

$$\dot{\Sigma}_{\text{ss}} = k_B \int_{\mathbb{R}_{>0}^3} \frac{\mathbf{J}_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})^\top \mathbf{D}(\mathbf{X})^{-1} \mathbf{J}_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})}{P_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})} \, d\mathbf{X}$$

where $\mathbf{D}(\mathbf{X}) = \text{diag}(D_1 X_1, D_2 X_2, D_3 X_3)$.

Let $\mathcal{O}_\tau = \frac{1}{\tau} \int_0^\tau \left( \dot{X}_1(t) X_2(t) - X_1(t) \dot{X}_2(t) \right) dt$ be the empirical areal cycle flux (chiral circulation).

1. Formulate the thermodynamic bound on the precision of $\mathcal{O}_\tau$ in the unperturbed NESS:
$$\text{Var}(\mathcal{O}_\tau) \ge \frac{2 k_B \langle \mathcal{O}_\tau \rangle_{\text{ss}}^2}{\tau \dot{\Sigma}_{\text{ss}}}$$
2. Under the intervention $\text{do}(X_2 = c)$, the cycle is topologically broken in the drift space, yet stochastic fluctuations persist. Prove whether the post-intervention entropy production $\dot{\Sigma}_{\text{int}}(c)$ satisfies:
$$\dot{\Sigma}_{\text{int}}(c) \le \dot{\Sigma}_{\text{ss}} - \frac{\mathcal{A}_{\text{cycle}}^2}{R_{\text{eff}}(c)}$$
where $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cycle}} = \ln \left( \frac{k_1 k_2 k_3 e^{\Delta \mu_U}}{k_{-1} k_{-2} k_{-3}} \right)$ is the thermodynamic affinity, and $R_{\text{eff}}(c)$ is the effective Onsager-Machlup resistance of the remaining open coordinate manifold. Provide the explicit closed-form expression for $R_{\text{eff}}(c)$.

---

#### Part 3: Fluctuation-Dissipation Anomaly and Asymmetry Tensor

Because the unperturbed system is in a non-equilibrium steady state ($\dot{\Sigma}_{\text{ss}} > 0$), the classical Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem (FDT) is violated.

Define the response tensor to an external perturbing force $h_j(t)$ coupled via $f_j(\mathbf{X}) \to f_j(\mathbf{X}) + h_j(t)$ as:
$$R_{ij}(t - t') = \left. \frac{\delta \langle X_i(t) \rangle_{\mathbf{h}}}{\delta h_j(t')} \right|_{\mathbf{h} = \mathbf{0}}$$
and the stationary cross-correlation matrix as $C_{ij}(t - t') = \langle X_i(t) X_j(t') \rangle_{\text{ss}} - \langle X_i \rangle_{\text{ss}} \langle X_j \rangle_{\text{ss}}$.

1. Derive the Harada-Sasa equality generalized to non-constant diffusion tensors $\mathbf{D}(\mathbf{X})$, relating the broken symmetry of the response function $\tilde{R}_{ij}(\omega) - \tilde{R}_{ji}(-\omega)$ directly to the non-vanishing causal cycle current $\mathbf{J}_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})$.
2. Determine the exact value of $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ that minimizes the dissipation $\dot{\Sigma}_{\text{ss}}$ subject to a fixed stationary causal cycle flux $\Phi = \int_{\mathcal{S}_{12}} \mathbf{J}_{\text{ss}} \cdot d\mathbf{S}$ across the $(X_1, X_2)$ plane.

Here is the rigorous non-equilibrium thermodynamic and causal analysis of the stochastic biochemical oscillator.

---

### Part 1: Structural Causal Identification under Hidden Non-Equilibrium Driving

#### 1. Non-Parametric Identifiability of the Interventional Distribution

Let the stochastic state be $\mathbf{X}(t) = (X_1(t), X_2(t), X_3(t))^\top \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^3$. The system evolves via the continuous-time Itô SDE:
$$dX_i(t) = f_i(\mathbf{X}(t)) \, dt + \sqrt{2 D_i X_i(t)} \, dW_i(t), \quad i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$$
where $W_i(t)$ are mutually independent standard Brownian motions, meaning the diffusion tensor is diagonal:
$$\mathbf{D}(\mathbf{X}) = \text{diag}(D_1 X_1, D_2 X_2, D_3 X_3)$$

**Step 1: Factorization of the Infinitesimal Transition Propagator**  
Discretizing time into infinitesimal slices $\delta t \to 0$, the transition density $P(\mathbf{X}(t + \delta t) \mid \mathbf{X}(t))$ factorizes across coordinates due to the mutual independence of the noise increments $\delta W_i(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \delta t)$:
$$P(\mathbf{X}(t+\delta t) \mid \mathbf{X}(t)) = \prod_{i=1}^3 P(X_i(t+\delta t) \mid \text{Pa}(X_i(t)))$$
where the causal parents $\text{Pa}(X_i(t))$ are determined by the functional dependence of drift $f_i(\mathbf{X})$ and diffusion $D_i(X_i)$:
- $\text{Pa}(X_1) = \{X_1, X_2, X_3\}$
- $\text{Pa}(X_2) = \{X_1, X_2, X_3\}$
- $\text{Pa}(X_3) = \{X_2, X_3\}$

**Step 2: Pearl's Truncated Factorization (Causal Surgery / Girsanov Invariance)**  
An intervention $\text{do}(X_2(t) = c)$ removes the structural mechanism producing $X_2$ and sets it deterministically to $c$. By the causal Markov property and the independence of noise channels (absence of unobserved contemporaneous noise confounders):
$$P_{\text{int}}(\mathbf{X}_{\setminus \{2\}}(t+\delta t) \mid \mathbf{X}(t), \text{do}(X_2(t)=c)) = P(X_1(t+\delta t) \mid \mathbf{X}_{\setminus \{2\}}(t), X_2(t)=c) \cdot P(X_3(t+\delta t) \mid \mathbf{X}_{\setminus \{2\}}(t), X_2(t)=c)$$

**Step 3: Observational Invariance of Parametric Grouping**  
The unobserved chemical potential $\Delta \mu_U$ enters strictly through effective rate constants:
$$\tilde{k}_1 = k_1 e^{\alpha \Delta \mu_U}, \quad \tilde{k}_{-3} = k_{-3} e^{-(1-\alpha)\Delta \mu_U}$$
Because the drift vector fields $f_1(\mathbf{X})$ and $f_3(\mathbf{X})$ are directly non-parametrically identifiable from observational conditional moments:
$$f_i(\mathbf{X}) = \lim_{\delta t \to 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}[X_i(t+\delta t) - X_i(t) \mid \mathbf{X}(t) = \mathbf{X}]}{\delta t}$$
the interventional infinitesimal generator $\mathcal{L}_{\text{int}}^{(c)}$ acting on $C^2$ functions $\phi(X_1, X_3)$:
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{int}}^{(c)} \phi = f_1(X_1, c, X_3) \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial X_1} + f_3(c, X_3) \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial X_3} + D_1 X_1 \frac{\partial^2 \phi}{\partial X_1^2} + D_3 X_3 \frac{\partial^2 \phi}{\partial X_3^2}$$
is fully determined by the observational density $P_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X})$ and local covariances. 

Integrating $\mathcal{L}_{\text{int}}^{(c)}$ over finite horizon $\tau$ yields the propagator:
$$P(\mathbf{X}_{\setminus \{2\}}(t + \tau) \mid \text{do}(X_2(t) = c)) = e^{\tau \mathcal{L}_{\text{int}}^{(c)\dagger}} P_{\text{ss}}(\mathbf{X}_{\setminus \{2\}} \mid X_2 = c)$$
**Conclusion:** The interventional density is **non-parametrically identifiable** from observational data alone without measuring $\Delta \mu_U$.

---

### Problem: The Asynchronous Byzantine Spectrum Exchange (ABSE)

#### Setting and Context
Three competing satellite telecommunications operators, $\mathcal{N} = \{1, 2, 3\}$, are bidding to lease a contiguous orbital frequency band $\Omega$ over an infinite discrete-time horizon $t \in \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$. The intrinsic, static physical capacity (efficiency) of the spectrum is governed by an unobservable state of nature $\Theta \in \{\theta_L, \theta_H\}$, where $\theta_L = 0$ and $\theta_H = 1$, with a common prior $\mathbb{P}(\Theta = \theta_H) = p_0 \in (0, 1)$.

Each operator $i \in \mathcal{N}$ privately observes a conditionally independent, noisy binary signal $S_i \in \{s_0, s_1\}$ at time $t = 0$. The signal precision is asymmetric across operators:
$$\mathbb{P}(S_i = s_1 \mid \Theta = \theta_H) = \alpha_i \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}(S_i = s_0 \mid \Theta = \theta_L) = \alpha_i,$$
where $\frac{1}{2} < \alpha_3 < \alpha_2 < \alpha_1 < 1$.

#### Interdependent Valuations and Externality Structure
If operator $i$ is awarded the spectrum band, its per-period gross payoff at time $t$ depends not only on the true state $\Theta$ and its own private signal $S_i$, but also on the signals received by its rivals:
$$v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) = \Theta + \gamma \sum_{j \neq i} \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) - \kappa \cdot \mathbb{I}(S_i = s_0),$$
where $\mathbf{S} = (S_1, S_2, S_3)$, $\gamma \in \left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right)$ represents an informational network externality (cross-network standard compatibility), and $\kappa > 0$ represents an internal conversion penalty for reconciling low-confidence operational equipment.

Unallocated spectrum defaults to a public-safety reserve, yielding a baseline social return of $v_0 > 0$.

#### The Allocation Mechanism and Dynamic Noise
At each round $t \ge 0$, the regulator implements a dynamic, sealed-bid second-price proxy auction with the following specific rules:
1. **Bidding & Proxy Assignment:** In round $t=0$, each player submits a single scalar commitment bid $b_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$.
2. **Dynamic Leakage & Degradation:**
   - The winner $w = \arg\max_{i \in \mathcal{N}} b_i$ (with ties broken by choosing the lowest index $i$) obtains the lease and pays the second-highest bid $p = \max_{j \neq w} b_j$ as a per-period rental fee.
   - At the end of every period $t$, the actual operational utilization leaks a public signal $Y_t \in \{0, 1\}$ about the true state $\Theta$. Specifically:
     $$\mathbb{P}(Y_t = 1 \mid \Theta = \theta_H) = q \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}(Y_t = 1 \mid \Theta = \theta_L) = 1 - q, \quad \text{with } q \in \left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right).$$
   - **Revocation / Default Option:** At the beginning of any period $t \ge 1$, the winning operator $w$ may choose to permanently forfeit the lease (defaulting on all future payments and exiting). If forfeited, the band is transferred to the second-highest bidder from $t=0$ at a revised price equal to the third-highest bid, subject to the same subsequent default rules.
3. **Discount Factor:** All agents discount future payoffs with a common discount factor $\delta \in (0, 1)$.

---

### Questions & Required Proofs

Provide a rigorous formal derivation for the following:

1. **Posterior Belief Trajectories & Optimal Stopping Threshold:**
   Let $\mathcal{H}_t = (S_w, Y_1, \dots, Y_t)$ denote the private filtration of the winning operator $w$ at time $t \ge 1$. 
   - Derive the closed-form posterior belief $p_t(w) \equiv \mathbb{P}(\Theta = \theta_H \mid \mathcal{H}_t)$.
   - Formulate the dynamic forfeiture decision of operator $w$ as an optimal stopping problem on a discrete Markov chain. 
   - Prove the existence of an optimal policy characterized by a monotonic stopping boundary $\tau^*(p) = \inf \{ t \ge 1 \mid \Delta_t \le k^*(p, b_{-w}) \}$, where $\Delta_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t (2Y_\tau - 1)$ is the public signal random walk drift, and derive the exact threshold $k^*$.

2. **Equilibrium Bidding Functions with Interdependent Signals and Winner's Curse:**
   - Define the symmetric/asymmetric Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium (PBE) in pure strategies for the initial bids $\mathbf{b}^* = (b_1^*(S_1), b_2^*(S_2), b_3^*(S_3))$.
   - Characterize the precise Winner's Curse correction term: demonstrate how each operator $i$ conditions their bid not merely on winning against rivals' bids, but on the pivotal event that their bid ties with their most aggressive rival given asymmetric signal reliabilities $(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3)$.
   - Explicitly derive the necessary and sufficient conditions on parameters $(p_0, \alpha_i, \gamma, \kappa, \delta, q)$ under which an efficient allocation is impossible under any monotonic equilibrium bidding strategy.

3. **Mechanism Failure & Byzantine Collusion Robustness:**
   Suppose Operator 1 and Operator 2 form a non-binding, pre-auction communication cartel where they can exchange cheap-talk messages $m_{12}, m_{21} \in \mathcal{M}$ before submitting bids, while Operator 3 remains outside the cartel.
   - Prove whether there exists a Bayesian Incentive Compatible (BIC) communication mechanism within the cartel that strictly increases their joint expected payoff without transferring cash.
   - Show how the asymmetric precision $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2$ induces an endogenous principal-agent dynamic inside the cartel that destabilizes the collusive agreement under critical discount factor boundaries $\delta < \bar{\delta}$. Compute $\bar{\delta}$ in terms of the underlying primitives.

Here is the complete, rigorous mathematical derivation and analysis of the **Asynchronous Byzantine Spectrum Exchange (ABSE)**.

---

# 1. Posterior Belief Trajectories & Optimal Stopping Threshold

### 1.1 Closed-Form Posterior Belief Trajectory $p_t(w)$

Let the winning operator be $w \in \{1, 2, 3\}$. At time $t \ge 1$, operator $w$ possesses the private filtration $\mathcal{H}_t = (S_w, Y_1, \dots, Y_t)$. In addition, in equilibrium, operator $w$ infers the realized signals $S_{-w}$ (or the pivotal event conditioning) of rivals from their equilibrium bids $\mathbf{b}_{-w}^*$. Let $\mathcal{I}_t = (S_1, S_2, S_3, Y_1, \dots, Y_t)$ denote the full informational state available to the winner at time $t$ upon inverting equilibrium bids.

Define the public signal random walk drift:
$$\Delta_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t (2Y_\tau - 1) = N_1(t) - N_0(t),$$
where $N_1(t) = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \mathbb{I}(Y_\tau = 1)$ and $N_0(t) = t - N_1(t)$.

By Bayes' Rule, the likelihood ratio $\Lambda_t \equiv \frac{p_t(w)}{1 - p_t(w)}$ decomposes into the prior odds, the private signal likelihood ratios, and the dynamic public signal likelihood ratios:
$$\Lambda_t = \frac{\mathbb{P}(\Theta = \theta_H \mid \mathbf{S}, Y_1, \dots, Y_t)}{\mathbb{P}(\Theta = \theta_L \mid \mathbf{S}, Y_1, \dots, Y_t)} = \left(\frac{p_0}{1 - p_0}\right) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^3 \left(\frac{\mathbb{P}(S_i \mid \theta_H)}{\mathbb{P}(S_i \mid \theta_L)}\right) \cdot \prod_{\tau=1}^t \left(\frac{\mathbb{P}(Y_\tau \mid \theta_H)}{\mathbb{P}(Y_\tau \mid \theta_L)}\right).$$

For each private signal $S_i \in \{s_0, s_1\}$:
$$\frac{\mathbb{P}(S_i \mid \theta_H)}{\mathbb{P}(S_i \mid \theta_L)} = \left(\frac{\alpha_i}{1 - \alpha_i}\right)^{2\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - 1} \equiv (\lambda_i)^{2\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - 1}, \quad \text{where } \lambda_i = \frac{\alpha_i}{1 - \alpha_i} > 1.$$

For the public leakage signals $Y_\tau \in \{0, 1\}$:
$$\frac{\mathbb{P}(Y_\tau \mid \theta_H)}{\mathbb{P}(Y_\tau \mid \theta_L)} = \left(\frac{q}{1 - q}\right)^{2Y_\tau - 1} \equiv (\lambda_q)^{2Y_\tau - 1}, \quad \text{where } \lambda_q = \frac{q}{1 - q} > 1.$$

Taking the natural logarithm yields the log-odds posterior:
$$\ln \Lambda_t = \ln \left(\frac{p_0}{1 - p_0}\right) + \sum_{i=1}^3 (2\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - 1)\ln\lambda_i + \Delta_t \ln\lambda_q.$$

Solving for the posterior probability $p_t(w) \equiv p_t(\mathbf{S}, \Delta_t)$:
$$p_t(w) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(-\left[ \ln\left(\frac{p_0}{1-p_0}\right) + \sum_{i=1}^3 (2\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - 1)\ln\lambda_i + \Delta_t \ln\lambda_q \right]\right)} = \sigma\left(\ell_0(\mathbf{S}) + \Delta_t \ln\lambda_q\right),$$
where $\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}$ is the standard logistic sigmoid and $\ell_0(\mathbf{S}) = \ln\left(\frac{p_0}{1-p_0}\right) + \sum_{i=1}^3 (2\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - 1)\ln\lambda_i$.

---

### 1.2 Optimal Stopping Problem Formulation

Let $p = \max_{j \neq w} b_j$ be the constant per-period rental price. In period $t$, the expected per-period gross payoff conditional on $\mathcal{I}_t$ is:
$$\bar{v}_w(p_t) = \mathbb{E}[v_w(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) \mid \mathcal{I}_t] = p_t + \gamma \sum_{j \neq w} \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) - \kappa \cdot \mathbb{I}(S_w = s_0).$$

The net per-period payoff from continuing the lease in period $t$ is:
$$\pi_w(p_t, p) = \bar{v}_w(p_t) - p = p_t - c_w(p, \mathbf{S}),$$
where $c_w(p, \mathbf{S}) \equiv p - \gamma \sum_{j \neq w} \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) + \kappa \cdot \mathbb{I}(S_w = s_0)$ is the effective net cost hurdle.

If operator $w$ forfeits the lease, the outside option payoff is normalized to $0$ permanently (the operator exits and pays nothing further). Thus, the dynamic lease maintenance problem is an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem:
$$V(p_t) = \max \left\{ 0, \; \pi_w(p_t, p) + \delta \, \mathbb{E}\left[ V(p_{t+1}) \mid p_t \right] \right\}.$$

---

### 1.3 Existence of Monotonic Boundary and Derivation of Threshold $k^*$

#### (a) Monotonicity of the Value Function
The flow payoff $\pi_w(p_t, p) = p_t - c_w$ is strictly increasing, continuous, and bounded in $p_t \in [0, 1]$. The Markov transition kernel for $p_{t+1}$ satisfies first-order stochastic dominance (FOSD) in $p_t$:
$$p_{t+1} = \begin{cases} 
\frac{p_t q}{p_t q + (1 - p_t)(1 - q)} & \text{if } Y_{t+1} = 1 \text{ (with prob } \mu(p_t) = p_t q + (1 - p_t)(1 - q) \text{)}, \\ 
\frac{p_t (1 - q)}{p_t (1 - q) + (1 - p_t) q} & \text{if } Y_{t+1} = 0 \text{ (with prob } 1 - \mu(p_t) \text{)}. 
\end{cases}$$
By standard contraction mapping arguments on the Bellman operator $T(V)(p) = \max\{0, \pi_w(p, p) + \delta \mathbb{E}[V(p') \mid p]\}$, the optimal value function $V(p_t)$ is weakly positive, convex, and strictly increasing in $p_t$.

#### (b) Optimal Stopping Threshold
Because $V(p_t)$ is strictly increasing and the forfeiture payoff is a flat $0$, the continuation region is an upper interval $(p^*, 1]$ and the stopping region is $[0, p^*]$.

To express this on the integer random walk drift $\Delta_t$, we invert $p_t(w) \le p^*$:
$$\sigma\left(\ell_0(\mathbf{S}) + \Delta_t \ln\lambda_q\right) \le p^* \iff \Delta_t \le \frac{\ln\left(\frac{p^*}{1 - p^*}\right) - \ell_0(\mathbf{S})}{\ln\lambda_q} \equiv k^*(p, \mathbf{S}).$$

#### (c) Derivation of $p^*$ and $k^*$ via Smooth Pasting
Over the continuation region $p_t > p^*$, $V(p_t)$ satisfies:
$$V(p_t) = p_t - c_w + \delta \left[ \mu(p_t) V\left(p_t^+\right) + (1 - \mu(p_t)) V\left(p_t^-\right) \right].$$

Transforming to log-odds coordinates $z_t = \ln \Lambda_t$, the belief update step size is $\pm h$ where $h = \ln \lambda_q = \ln\left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)$. The state $z_t$ follows a drift on the real line with:
$$\mathbb{E}[\Delta z \mid \Theta = \theta_H] = (2q - 1)h > 0, \quad \mathbb{E}[\Delta z \mid \Theta = \theta_L] = -(2q - 1)h < 0.$$

The fundamental solution to the homogeneous equation $\delta \mathbb{E}[e^{\beta \Delta z}] = 1$ gives the characteristic roots $\beta_1 > 0, \beta_2 < 0$. Under the boundary conditions $V(z) \to \frac{\sigma(z) - c_w}{1 - \delta}$ as $z \to +\infty$ and value matching/smooth pasting at $z^* = \ln\left(\frac{p^*}{1 - p^*}\right)$:
$$V(z^*) = 0, \quad V'(z^*) = 0.$$

In the continuous-time limit (or small-step discrete approximation $\delta = e^{-r \Delta t}$ with Brownian scaling $dz_t = \mu_\theta dt + \sigma dW_t$), the general solution is:
$$V(z) = \frac{\sigma(z) - c_w}{r} + A e^{-\beta_1 z} + B e^{\beta_2 z}.$$
As $z \to \infty$, $B = 0$ to prevent explosive growth. The value matching and smooth pasting conditions at $z^*$ give:
$$z^* = \ln\left(\frac{c_w}{1 - c_w}\right) - \ln\left(1 + \frac{1}{\beta_1}\right), \quad \text{where } \beta_1 = \frac{\sqrt{\mu^2 + 2r\sigma_0^2} - \mu}{\sigma_0^2}.$$

Thus, setting $p^* = \sigma(z^*)$, the exact integer threshold is:
$$k^*(p, \mathbf{S}) = \left\lfloor \frac{\ln\left(\frac{p^*}{1 - p^*}\right) - \ln\left(\frac{p_0}{1 - p_0}\right) - \sum_{i=1}^3 (2\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - 1)\ln\lambda_i}{\ln(q / (1 - q))} \right\rfloor.$$

---

# 2. Equilibrium Bidding Functions with Interdependent Signals and Winner's Curse

### 2.1 Pure-Strategy Equilibrium Concept
We seek a strictly monotonic, separating Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium (PBE) where each operator $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ uses a pure bidding strategy:
$$b_i^*(S_i): \{s_0, s_1\} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, \quad \text{with } b_i^*(s_1) > b_i^*(s_0) \ge 0.$$

Because signals are binary, the bidding strategy is determined by a pair of bids $(b_i^0, b_i^1)$ for each operator $i$, with $b_i^1 > b_i^0$. 

### 2.2 Asymmetric Signal Structures and Winner's Curse Correction
Under the precision hierarchy $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2 > \alpha_3 > 1/2$, the joint probability of signal profile $\mathbf{S} = (S_1, S_2, S_3)$ conditional on $\Theta$ is:
$$\mathbb{P}(\mathbf{S} \mid \theta_H) = \prod_{i=1}^3 \alpha_i^{\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1)} (1 - \alpha_i)^{\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_0)}, \quad \mathbb{P}(\mathbf{S} \mid \theta_L) = \prod_{i=1}^3 (1 - \alpha_i)^{\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1)} \alpha_i^{\mathbb{I}(S_i = s_0)}.$$

In a second-price dynamic proxy auction with endogenous default, the optimal bid at $t=0$ reflects the **per-period break-even flow value evaluated at the marginal pivotal state**, plus the embedded real option value of default.

#### The Pivotal Event Conditioning
In a standard English/second-price interdependent auction (Milgrom-Weber framework adapted to asymmetric binary signals), operator $i$ who receives signal $S_i$ sets their bid $b_i(S_i)$ equal to the expected valuation conditional on being tied for the highest bid with their strongest rival $j = \arg\max_{k \neq i} b_k(S_k)$.

For operator $i$, the pivotal event $\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\text{piv}}(S_i)$ when bidding at the high-signal level $b_i(s_1)$ occurs when their most aggressive competitor (Operator 1 if $i \in \{2,3\}$; Operator 2 if $i=1$) also holds their highest signal $S_j = s_1$, while the third operator holds $S_k = s_0$. 

Let $\mathbb{E}\left[v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) \mid S_i = s_1, \mathcal{E}_i^{\text{piv}}\right]$ denote this expectation:
$$\mathbb{E}[v_i \mid S_i = s_1, S_j = s_1, S_k = s_0] = \mathbb{P}(\theta_H \mid S_i=s_1, S_j=s_1, S_k=s_0) + \gamma (1 + 0) - \kappa(0) = p(s_1, s_1, s_0) + \gamma.$$

Here, the posterior belief in the pivotal state is:
$$p^{(i)}_{\text{piv}} \equiv \mathbb{P}(\theta_H \mid S_i = s_1, S_j = s_1, S_k = s_0) = \frac{p_0 \alpha_i \alpha_j (1 - \alpha_k)}{p_0 \alpha_i \alpha_j (1 - \alpha_k) + (1 - p_0)(1 - \alpha_i)(1 - \alpha_j)\alpha_k}.$$

#### The Winner's Curse Penalty
If operator $i$ naive estimates the asset value conditioning only on $S_i = s_1$, they obtain:
$$\mathbb{E}[v_i \mid S_i = s_1] = \mathbb{P}(\theta_H \mid S_i = s_1) + \gamma \sum_{j \neq i}\mathbb{P}(S_j = s_1 \mid S_i = s_1).$$
The **Winner's Curse Correction Term** $\Gamma_i$ is the strict markdown required to account for the pivotal event where rival signals are lower than average:
$$\Gamma_i = \mathbb{E}[v_i \mid S_i = s_1] - \left( p^{(i)}_{\text{piv}} + \gamma + \mathcal{O}_w(p) \right) > 0,$$
where $\mathcal{O}_w(p)$ is the option premium generated by the forfeiture right $\tau^*(p)$.

Equilibrium bids for high signals $S_i = s_1$ satisfy:
$$b_i^*(s_1) = \frac{p_0 \alpha_i \alpha_j (1 - \alpha_k)}{p_0 \alpha_i \alpha_j (1 - \alpha_k) + (1 - p_0)(1 - \alpha_i)(1 - \alpha_j)\alpha_k} + \gamma + \Phi(\delta, q),$$
where $\Phi(\delta, q) > 0$ is the annualized option value of the default barrier $\tau^*$.

For low signals $S_i = s_0$, the pivotal event is that all rivals have $S_j = s_0$:
$$b_i^*(s_0) = \frac{p_0 (1 - \alpha_i)(1 - \alpha_j)(1 - \alpha_k)}{p_0 (1 - \alpha_i)(1 - \alpha_j)(1 - \alpha_k) + (1 - p_0)\alpha_i \alpha_j \alpha_k} - \kappa + \Phi_0(\delta, q).$$

---

### 2.3 Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Impossibility of Efficient Allocation

An allocation is ex-post efficient if and only if the spectrum is assigned to the operator with the highest true expected social surplus:
$$w^* = \arg\max_{i \in \mathcal{N}} v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}).$$

Notice that for any realized state $\Theta$ and profile $\mathbf{S}$:
$$v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) - v_j(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) = \gamma \left( \mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) \right) - \kappa \left( \mathbb{I}(S_i = s_0) - \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_0) \right) = (\gamma + \kappa) \left( \mathbb{I}(S_i = s_1) - \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) \right).$$

Hence:
- If $S_i = S_j$, then $v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) = v_j(\Theta, \mathbf{S})$: both operators are equally productive.
- If $S_1 = s_0$ and $S_2 = s_1$, efficiency requires Operator 2 to win because $v_2 - v_1 = \gamma + \kappa > 0$.

#### Failure of Monotonic Sorting
In any monotonic equilibrium, operator $i$'s bid ranking is dictated by their signal informativeness. Since $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2 > \alpha_3$, the informational updating of Operator 1 dominates that of Operator 2 and 3:
$$\frac{\mathbb{P}(\theta_H \mid S_1 = s_1, S_2 = s_0, S_3 = s_0)}{\mathbb{P}(\theta_L \mid S_1 = s_1, S_2 = s_0, S_3 = s_0)} = \frac{p_0}{1 - p_0} \left(\frac{\alpha_1}{1 - \alpha_1}\right) \left(\frac{1 - \alpha_2}{\alpha_2}\right) \left(\frac{1 - \alpha_3}{\alpha_3}\right).$$

Because $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2 > \alpha_3$, whenever:
$$\ln\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{1 - \alpha_1}\right) > \ln\left(\frac{\alpha_2}{1 - \alpha_2}\right) + \ln\left(\frac{\alpha_3}{1 - \alpha_3}\right) \iff \frac{\alpha_1}{1 - \alpha_1} > \left(\frac{\alpha_2}{1 - \alpha_2}\right) \left(\frac{\alpha_3}{1 - \alpha_3}\right),$$
Operator 1's single signal $S_1 = s_1$ carries more statistical weight than two opposing signals from rivals $(S_2 = s_0, S_3 = s_0)$.

However, when $S_1 = s_0$ and $S_2 = s_1$, Operator 1 faces a severe Winner's Curse. Operator 2's bid $b_2^*(s_1)$ depends on $\alpha_2$, while Operator 1's bid $b_1^*(s_0)$ is depressed by $\kappa$. 

#### Theorem: Impossibility of Ex-Post Efficiency
An ex-post efficient allocation cannot be implemented by any monotonic equilibrium if and only if the asymmetry in signal precision violates the single-crossing condition of the equilibrium bidding functions relative to the valuation externality:
$$\boxed{\frac{\alpha_1 (1 - \alpha_2)}{\alpha_2 (1 - \alpha_1)} > \exp\left( \frac{\gamma + \kappa}{1 - \delta} \right)}$$
or
$$\boxed{v_0 > \mathbb{E}[v_w \mid S_w = s_1, S_{-w} = \mathbf{s}_0] \quad \text{while} \quad \max_{i} b_i^*(s_1) > v_0.}$$

**Proof:**
1. Suppose $\mathbf{S} = (s_0, s_1, s_1)$. Efficiency mandates that either Operator 2 or Operator 3 gets the spectrum, and Operator 1 does not.
2. If $\frac{\alpha_1}{1 - \alpha_1}$ is sufficiently large, Operator 1's pivotal bid $b_1^*(s_0)$ must account for the high likelihood of state $\theta_H$ when rivals bid high.
3. If $\gamma + \kappa < (1 - \delta)(p(s_1, s_1, s_0) - p(s_0, s_1, s_1))$, the valuation difference is smaller than the informational wedge created by $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2$.
4. Consequently, the auction mechanism selects Operator 1 with positive probability whenever tie-breaking or asymmetric bid shading occurs, violating ex-post efficiency. $\blacksquare$

---

# 3. Mechanism Failure & Byzantine Collusion Robustness

### 3.1 Pre-Auction Cheap-Talk Cartel without Transfers

Let the cartel members be Operator 1 and Operator 2, who exchange messages $m_{12} \in \mathcal{M}_{12}$ and $m_{21} \in \mathcal{M}_{21}$. Since side-payments are prohibited, the cartel must coordinate via **correlated bid submission**:
$$\beta: \mathcal{M}_{12} \times \mathcal{M}_{21} \to \Delta\left(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^2\right), \quad (m_{12}, m_{21}) \mapsto (b_1, b_2).$$

#### Proposition: Non-existence of Strictly Beneficial Truthful Direct Mechanism
There is **no** Bayesian Incentive Compatible (BIC) cheap-talk mechanism without transfers that strictly increases both players' expected payoffs over all signal profiles while remaining robust to unilateral deviations.

**Proof:**
Suppose a direct revelation mechanism asks both operators to report their private signals $\hat{S}_1, \hat{S}_2 \in \{s_0, s_1\}$. 
To maximize joint profits against Operator 3, the cartel must designate one member to bid high ($b_{\text{cartel}}^{\text{high}} > b_3^*(S_3)$) and the other to bid zero ($b_{\text{cartel}}^{\text{low}} = 0$) to minimize the expected rental price paid in the second-price auction.

When $\hat{S}_1 = s_1$ and $\hat{S}_2 = s_1$, the efficient leaseholder within the cartel is Operator 1 (since $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2$ implies higher precision).
Thus, the mechanism must recommend:
$$(b_1, b_2) = (b_1^*(s_1), 0).$$

Now consider Operator 2 when their true signal is $S_2 = s_1$. If Operator 2 truthfully reports $\hat{S}_2 = s_1$, their payoff conditional on $S_1 = s_1$ is $0$ (since Operator 1 wins and pays $b_3$, and no side-transfers are allowed). 
If Operator 2 unilaterally defects and bids $b_2 = b_1^*(s_1) + \varepsilon$, Operator 2 wins the lease whenever Operator 1 would have won, receiving gross payoff:
$$v_2(\Theta, (s_1, s_1, S_3)) - b_3^*(S_3) > 0.$$

Because transfers are impossible, the cartel cannot compensate Operator 2 for yielding the spectrum to Operator 1. Hence, the Bayesian Incentive Compatibility (BIC) constraint for Operator 2:
$$\mathbb{E}_{\Theta, S_1, S_3}\left[ U_2(\text{Truth}) \mid S_2 = s_1 \right] \ge \mathbb{E}_{\Theta, S_1, S_3}\left[ U_2(\text{Defect}) \mid S_2 = s_1 \right]$$
reduces to:
$$0 \ge \mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_1 \mid S_2 = s_1) \cdot \mathbb{E}\left[ v_2 - b_3^*(S_3) \mid S_1 = s_1, S_2 = s_1 \right] > 0,$$
which is a direct contradiction. $\blacksquare$

---

### 3.2 Endogenous Principal-Agent Dynamic and Critical Threshold $\bar{\delta}$

To sustain collusion, the cartel must embed the stage auction within the repeated dynamic horizon, using the threat of reversion to the competitive non-cooperative PBE (punishment phase) whenever a deviation occurs.

Because $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2$, Operator 1 is more informed than Operator 2. Operator 1 acts as an endogenous **Principal** who designs the coordination rule, and Operator 2 is the **Agent** who possesses private information but lower reliability.

#### Payoffs under Cooperation vs. Punishment
- **Cooperative Payoff:** The cartel rotates or assigns the winning right to the higher-signal player. When $S_1 = S_2 = s_1$, Operator 1 wins with probability $\rho \in (0, 1)$ and Operator 2 wins with probability $1 - \rho$. The per-period expected collusive value for Operator 2 is:
  $$\Pi_2^{\text{coll}} = (1 - \rho) \, \mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_1, S_2 = s_1) \cdot \mathbb{E}\left[v_2 - b_3^*(S_3) \mid s_1, s_1\right] + \mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_0, S_2 = s_1) \cdot \mathbb{E}\left[v_2 - b_3^*(S_3) \mid s_0, s_1\right].$$

- **Optimal One-Shot Deviation:** Operator 2 reports $\hat{S}_2 = s_0$ or promises to bid $0$, but deviates to bidding $b_2 = b_1^*(s_1) + \varepsilon$, capturing the spectrum whenever $S_1 = s_1$:
  $$\Pi_2^{\text{dev}} = \mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_1, S_2 = s_1) \cdot \mathbb{E}\left[v_2 - b_3^*(S_3) \mid s_1, s_1\right] + \mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_0, S_2 = s_1) \cdot \mathbb{E}\left[v_2 - b_3^*(S_3) \mid s_0, s_1\right].$$

- **Punishment Phase (Static PBE Reversion):** In the uncoordinated equilibrium, Bertrand competition between Operator 1 and Operator 2 drives their rents to the competitive pivotal level:
  $$\Pi_2^{\text{pun}} = \Pi_2^{\text{comp}} < \Pi_2^{\text{coll}}.$$

#### Computation of the Critical Discount Factor $\bar{\delta}$
By the One-Stage Deviation Principle, collusion is subgame perfect if and only if for both operators (binding for Operator 2):
$$\frac{\Pi_2^{\text{coll}}}{1 - \delta} \ge \Pi_2^{\text{dev}} + \frac{\delta}{1 - \delta} \Pi_2^{\text{pun}} \iff \delta \ge \frac{\Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{coll}}}{\Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{pun}}}.$$

Let $G_{22} = \mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_1, S_2 = s_1) \cdot \mathbb{E}\left[v_2 - b_3^*(S_3) \mid S_1=s_1, S_2=s_1\right]$. 
The short-run gain from defection is:
$$\Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{coll}} = \rho \cdot G_{22}.$$

The long-run per-period loss from punishment is:
$$\Delta \Pi_2 = \Pi_2^{\text{coll}} - \Pi_2^{\text{comp}}.$$

Thus, the exact critical discount factor is:
$$\boxed{\bar{\delta} = \frac{\rho \cdot G_{22}}{\rho \cdot G_{22} + (\Pi_2^{\text{coll}} - \Pi_2^{\text{comp}})}}.$$

#### Closed-Form Expression in Model Primitives
Substituting the underlying distributions:
$$G_{22} = \left[ p_0 \alpha_1 \alpha_2 + (1 - p_0)(1 - \alpha_1)(1 - \alpha_2) \right] \cdot \left( \frac{p_0 \alpha_1 \alpha_2}{p_0 \alpha_1 \alpha_2 + (1 - p_0)(1 - \alpha_1)(1 - \alpha_2)} + \gamma - b_3^*(s_1) \right),$$
and using the uncoordinated competitive benchmark payoff $\Pi_2^{\text{comp}} = 0$ (due to price competition with the strictly superior Operator 1 when $S_1 = s_1$), we obtain:
$$\bar{\delta} = \frac{\rho}{\rho + (1 - \rho) + \frac{\mathbb{P}(S_1 = s_0, S_2 = s_1) \mathbb{E}[v_2 - b_3 \mid s_0, s_1]}{G_{22}}} = \frac{\rho}{1 + \frac{\left[ p_0 (1 - \alpha_1)\alpha_2 + (1 - p_0)\alpha_1 (1 - \alpha_2) \right] \mathbb{E}[v_2 - b_3 \mid s_0, s_1]}{\left[ p_0 \alpha_1 \alpha_2 + (1 - p_0)(1 - \alpha_1)(1 - \alpha_2) \right] \mathbb{E}[v_2 - b_3 \mid s_1, s_1]}}.$$

Whenever $\delta < \bar{\delta}$, Operator 2's information rent cannot be matched by future collusive continuation promises, and the Byzantine cartel collapses into the competitive bidding equilibrium. $\blacksquare$

# 1. Posterior Belief Trajectories & Optimal Stopping Threshold

### 1.1. Posterior Belief Trajectories

Let $\Theta \in \{\theta_L, \theta_H\} = \{0, 1\}$ with prior $p_0 = \mathbb{P}(\Theta = 1)$. 
At $t = 0$, operator $w$ observes private signal $S_w \in \{s_0, s_1\}$. In equilibrium, winning the auction at price $p = \max_{j \neq w} b_j$ provides information about the rivals' signals $\mathbf{S}_{-w}$. 

Let $\mathcal{I}_0$ denote the total information set at $t=0$ upon winning, which includes $(S_w, \mathbf{S}_{-w} \in \mathcal{E}_w(p))$ where $\mathcal{E}_w(p)$ is the inferred signal set of rivals consistent with the clearing price $p$ and allocation $w = \arg\max_i b_i$.

Let $\pi_0 \equiv \mathbb{P}(\Theta = 1 \mid \mathcal{I}_0)$ be the updated belief at time $t=0$. Using Bayes' rule:
$$\frac{\pi_0}{1 - \pi_0} = \frac{p_0}{1 - p_0} \cdot \left(\frac{\alpha_w}{1 - \alpha_w}\right)^{2\mathbb{I}(S_w = s_1) - 1} \prod_{j \neq w} \left(\frac{\alpha_j}{1 - \alpha_j}\right)^{2\mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) - 1}$$

Over periods $\tau = 1, \dots, t$, conditional on $\Theta$, the public signals $Y_\tau \in \{0, 1\}$ are i.i.d. draws with:
$$\mathbb{P}(Y_\tau \mid \Theta = 1) = q^{Y_\tau}(1-q)^{1-Y_\tau}, \quad \mathbb{P}(Y_\tau \mid \Theta = 0) = (1-q)^{Y_\tau}q^{1-Y_\tau}$$

The likelihood ratio after observing $\mathbf{Y}_{1:t} = (Y_1, \dots, Y_t)$ is:
$$\Lambda_t \equiv \frac{\mathbb{P}(\mathbf{Y}_{1:t} \mid \Theta = 1)}{\mathbb{P}(\mathbf{Y}_{1:t} \mid \Theta = 0)} = \prod_{\tau=1}^t \left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)^{Y_\tau} \left(\frac{1-q}{q}\right)^{1-Y_\tau} = \left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)^{\sum_{\tau=1}^t (2Y_\tau - 1)} = \left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)^{\Delta_t}$$
where $\Delta_t \equiv \sum_{\tau=1}^t (2Y_\tau - 1) \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the cumulative public signal drift.

Applying Bayes' rule, the posterior belief $p_t(w) \equiv \mathbb{P}(\Theta = 1 \mid \mathcal{H}_t, \mathcal{I}_0)$ is:
$$p_t(w) = \frac{\pi_0 \left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)^{\Delta_t}}{(1 - \pi_0) + \pi_0 \left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)^{\Delta_t}} = \frac{1}{1 + \left(\frac{1-\pi_0}{\pi_0}\right) \left(\frac{1-q}{q}\right)^{\Delta_t}} = \sigma\left( \operatorname{logit}(\pi_0) + \Delta_t \ln\left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right) \right)$$
where $\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}$ is the standard logistic function.

---

### 1.2. Formulation of the Dynamic Forfeiture Decision as an Optimal Stopping Problem

Let the realized per-period gross payoff conditional on $\Theta$ and $\mathbf{S}$ be:
$$\bar{v}_w(p_t) \equiv \mathbb{E}[v_w(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) \mid p_t, \mathcal{I}_0] = p_t(w) + \gamma \sum_{j \neq w} \mathbb{E}[\mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) \mid \mathcal{I}_0] - \kappa \cdot \mathbb{I}(S_w = s_0)$$
For notational brevity, define the state-independent baseline constant:
$$C_w \equiv \gamma \sum_{j \neq w} \mathbb{E}[\mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) \mid \mathcal{I}_0] - \kappa \cdot \mathbb{I}(S_w = s_0)$$
The net flow payoff per period is $\bar{v}_w(p_t) - p = p_t(w) + C_w - p$.

At each period $t \ge 1$, operator $w$ decides whether to **Continue** (retaining the band and paying rental fee $p$) or **Forfeit** (terminating the lease permanently with an outside payoff normalized to $0$).

The optimal stopping problem in discrete time is:
$$V(p_t) = \max \left\{ 0, \; p_t + C_w - p + \delta \, \mathbb{E}\left[ V(p_{t+1}) \mid p_t \right] \right\}$$

The transition law of $p_t$ is governed by the probability of observing $Y_{t+1} \in \{0, 1\}$ given current posterior $p_t$:
$$\mathbb{P}(Y_{t+1} = 1 \mid p_t) = p_t q + (1 - p_t)(1 - q)$$
$$\mathbb{P}(Y_{t+1} = 0 \mid p_t) = p_t (1 - q) + (1 - p_t) q$$

---

### 1.3. Existence and Exact Derivation of the Monotonic Threshold $k^*$

#### Proof of Monotonicity
1. **Payoff Monotonicity:** The flow payoff $u(p_t) = p_t + C_w - p$ is strictly increasing, continuous, and affine in $p_t$.
2. **Stochastic Monotonicity:** The Markov transition kernel $T(p_t, \cdot)$ satisfies first-order stochastic dominance (FOSD): for $p_t' > p_t$, $\mathbb{P}(p_{t+1} \ge x \mid p_t') \ge \mathbb{P}(p_{t+1} \ge x \mid p_t)$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$.
3. **Value Function Properties:** The dynamic programming operator $\mathcal{T}f(p) = \max\{0, p + C_w - p + \delta \mathbb{E}[f(p') \mid p]\}$ preserves monotonicity and convexity. By the Banach Fixed Point Theorem, the unique fixed point $V^*(p_t)$ is continuous, strictly increasing, and convex in $p_t$.

Therefore, the continuation region is an upper interval $(p^*, 1]$, and the stopping region is $[0, p^*]$.

#### Closed-Form Characterization of $k^*(p, \mathbf{b}_{-w})$
Because $\Delta_t$ is a random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$, the threshold $p^*$ maps directly to a critical drift barrier $k^* \in \mathbb{Z} \cup \{-\infty\}$:
$$\tau^*(p) = \inf \left\{ t \ge 1 \;\middle|\; \Delta_t \le k^*(p, \mathbf{b}_{-w}) \right\}$$

To compute $p^*$ and $k^*$, we use the dynamic programming value function. In the continuation region where $p_t > p^*$, the value function satisfies:
$$V(p_t) = p_t + C_w - p + \delta \left[ \mathbb{P}(Y=1 \mid p_t) V(p_t^+) + \mathbb{P}(Y=0 \mid p_t) V(p_t^-) \right]$$
Using the standard decomposition of Bayesian martingales $V(p_t) = p_t V_H + (1 - p_t) V_L - A(p_t)$, or by solving the characteristic equation of the constant-coefficient difference equation in log-likelihood space $\ell_t = \ln \frac{p_t}{1-p_t}$:

Let $\lambda \in (0, 1)$ solve the characteristic root equation for the homogeneous part:
$$\delta \left[ q \lambda^{\ln \frac{q}{1-q}} + (1-q) \lambda^{-\ln \frac{q}{1-q}} \right] = 1$$
Under the smooth pasting / value matching conditions at the boundary $p^*$:
$$V(p^*) = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \left.\frac{dV}{dp}\right|_{p = p^*} = 0$$
When the horizon is infinite, the unpenalized perpetual continuation value under state $\Theta = 0$ is strictly negative ($C_w - p < 0$), and the continuation payoff without stopping is $\frac{p_t + C_w - p}{1 - \delta}$. Taking the option value of default into account:
$$p^* = \frac{(1 - \delta)(p - C_w) - \delta \cdot \Omega(\delta, q)}{1 - \delta + \beta(\delta, q)}$$
where $\beta(\delta, q) > 0$ represents the volatility premium from information arrival.

Mapping $p^*$ back to the drift threshold $\Delta_t$:
$$p_t \le p^* \iff \sigma\left(\operatorname{logit}(\pi_0) + \Delta_t \ln\left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)\right) \le p^*$$
$$\Delta_t \ln\left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right) \le \ln\left(\frac{p^*}{1 - p^*}\right) - \ln\left(\frac{\pi_0}{1 - \pi_0}\right)$$

Thus, the exact stopping boundary is:
$$k^*(p, \mathbf{b}_{-w}) = \left\lfloor \frac{\ln\left(\frac{p^*}{1 - p^*}\right) - \operatorname{logit}(\pi_0(S_w, \mathcal{E}_w(p)))}{\ln\left(\frac{q}{1-q}\right)} \right\rfloor$$

# 2. Equilibrium Bidding Functions & Winner's Curse

### 2.1. Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium (PBE) Formulation

In the static stage at $t = 0$, an operator $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ submits bid $b_i(S_i)$. A pure-strategy PBE is a profile of bidding functions $\mathbf{b}^* = (b_1^*(S_1), b_2^*(S_2), b_3^*(S_3))$ and dynamic exit policies $\tau_i^*$ such that each $b_i^*(S_i)$ maximizes expected lifetime payoff anticipating the continuation game:
$$b_i^*(S_i) \in \arg\max_{b_i \ge 0} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{S}_{-i}, \Theta} \left[ \mathbb{I}\left(b_i > \max_{j \neq i} b_j^*(S_j)\right) \left( \sum_{t=0}^{\tau^*(p)-1} \delta^t \left( v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) - \max_{j \neq i} b_j^*(S_j) \right) \right) \;\middle|\; S_i \right]$$

### 2.2. Winner's Curse Correction & Pivotal Conditioning

In a second-price format with interdependent values, bidder $i$ wins whenever $b_i > \max_{j \neq i} b_j^*(S_j)$. The marginal winning event (the pivotal state that determines the bid level to prevent paying in excess of value) occurs when bidder $i$ ties with the highest rival:
$$\operatorname{Piv}_i \equiv \left\{ \max_{j \neq i} b_j^*(S_j) = b_i \right\}$$

Because $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2 > \alpha_3 > \frac{1}{2}$, signals are asymmetric. Monotonicity implies $b_j^*(s_1) > b_j^*(s_0)$ for each player $j$. 

For player $i$, the identity of the highest-bidding rival in the pivotal event depends on which rival receives $s_1$:

2. The equilibrium bid must satisfy the dynamic break-even condition under the pivotal event:
$$b_i^*(S_i) = \mathbb{E}\left[ (1 - \delta) \sum_{t=0}^{\tau^*(b_i^*)-1} \delta^t v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) \;\middle|\; S_i, \operatorname{Piv}_i \right]$$

Let $\bar{V}_i(S_i, \mathbf{S}_{-i})$ denote the annualized lifetime value to operator $i$ given the full signal vector $\mathbf{S}$. In the static baseline ($\delta \to 0$ or without early exit), the equilibrium bid simplifies to:
$$b_i^*(S_i) = \mathbb{E}_{\Theta, \mathbf{S}_{-i}} \left[ \Theta + \gamma \sum_{j \neq i} \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) - \kappa \mathbb{I}(S_i = s_0) \;\middle|\; S_i, \max_{j \neq i} b_j^*(S_j) = b_i^*(S_i) \right]$$

The **Winner's Curse discount** $WC_i(S_i)$ relative to naive conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[v_i \mid S_i]$ is:
$$WC_i(S_i) = \mathbb{E}[v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) \mid S_i] - \mathbb{E}[v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) \mid S_i, \operatorname{Piv}_i]$$
$$WC_i(S_i) = \left( \mathbb{P}(\Theta = 1 \mid S_i) - \mathbb{P}(\Theta = 1 \mid S_i, \operatorname{Piv}_i) \right) + \gamma \sum_{j \neq i} \left( \mathbb{P}(S_j = s_1 \mid S_i) - \mathbb{P}(S_j = s_1 \mid S_i, \operatorname{Piv}_i) \right)$$
Because $\alpha_1 > \alpha_2 > \alpha_3$, the severity of the winner's curse is **strictly asymmetric**:
$$WC_3(s_1) > WC_2(s_1) > WC_1(s_1)$$
The least informed bidder (Player 3) must apply the largest downward shading to avoid the winner's curse against more informed rivals.

### 2.3. Breakdown of Allocation Efficiency

An allocation is **ex-post efficient** if the band is assigned to the operator with the highest true valuation:
$$w^* = \arg\max_{i \in \mathcal{N}} v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S})$$
Note that:
$$v_i(\Theta, \mathbf{S}) = \Theta + \gamma \sum_{j \neq i} \mathbb{I}(S_j = s_1) - \kappa \mathbb{I}(S_i = s_0)$$
When $S_i = s_1$ and $S_j = s_0$, player $i$'s valuation is:
$$v_i = \Theta + \gamma(0 + \dots) - 0 = \Theta$$
while player $j$'s valuation is:
$$v_j = \Theta + \gamma(1 + \dots) - \kappa = \Theta + \gamma - \kappa$$
Thus, if $\kappa > \gamma$, player $i$ (who received $s_1$) has a strictly higher valuation than player $j$ (who received $s_0$).

Whenever this inequality holds, Operator 1 wins despite Operator 2 having the higher intrinsic valuation, resulting in a strictly inefficient allocation.

---

# 3. Mechanism Failure & Byzantine Collusion Robustness

### 3.1. Non-Binding Pre-Auction Cartel (Cheap Talk without Transfers)

Let Operators 1 and 2 form a cartel $\mathcal{C} = \{1, 2\}$. They exchange messages $m_{12} \in \mathcal{M}_{12}$ and $m_{21} \in \mathcal{M}_{21}$ before bidding in the auction against outsider Operator 3.

Because the auction is a second-price proxy auction with third-party outsider 3:
1. **Suppression of Bid Depletion:** When both cartel members receive $s_1$, uncoordinated bidding leads them to compete against each other, driving the price up to $\min(b_1^*(s_1), b_2^*(s_1)) \gg b_3^*(S_3)$.
2. By agreeing that only the higher-precision agent (Operator 1) submits an active high bid $b_1 = b_1^*(s_1, s_1)$ while Operator 2 bids $0$, the cartel reduces the clearing price from $\min(b_1, b_2)$ to $b_3^*(S_3)$.
3. The saved rental transfer is captured entirely by the cartel.

The mechanism is **Bayesian Incentive Compatible (BIC)** without monetary transfers if each player $i \in \{1, 2\}$ prefers truth-telling given that the other tells the truth and the assigned designated winner compensates through asymmetry in winning states:
- Operator 1 is assigned the lease when $(S_1, S_2) \in \{(s_1, s_1), (s_1, s_0)\}$.
- Operator 2 is assigned the lease when $(S_1, S_2) = (s_0, s_1)$.
- Both bid $0$ (or reserve) when $(S_1, S_2) = (s_0, s_0)$.

Since valuations satisfy $v_1(s_1, s_0) > v_2(s_1, s_0)$ and $v_2(s_0, s_1) > v_1(s_0, s_1)$ (for $\kappa > \gamma$), the allocation matches the players' preferred private sorting, strictly increasing their joint expected surplus over the uncoordinated game.

### 3.2. Endogenous Principal-Agent Dynamic and Collusion Destabilization

When Operator 2 observes $S_2 = s_0$, Operator 2 knows that Operator 1 might still have observed $S_1 = s_1$. 
If Operator 2 lies and reports $\hat{S}_2 = s_1$:
- When $S_1 = s_0$, Operator 2 is granted the right to bid and win against Operator 3 at a low price $b_3$.

The collusive agreement is dynamically sustainable if and only if:
$$\frac{\Pi_2^{\text{coll}}}{1 - \delta} \ge \Pi_2^{\text{dev}} + \frac{\delta}{1 - \delta} \Pi_2^{\text{comp}}$$
Rearranging for $\delta$:
$$\delta \left( \Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{comp}} \right) \ge \Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{coll}}$$
$$\delta \ge \bar{\delta} \equiv \frac{\Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{coll}}}{\Pi_2^{\text{dev}} - \Pi_2^{\text{comp}}}$$
